html:
The Nanticoke are an Algonquian people of the Delmarva Peninsula, on the eastern shore of Chesapeake Bay. Their name, Nentego, means "tidewater people". Their main towns stood along the Nanticoke River in present-day Maryland and Delaware.

They fished, gathered oysters, hunted and grew maize, and were known as makers of shell beads used in trade. In 1608 the English captain John Smith met them while exploring the Chesapeake. Their neighbours included the Accomack, the Pocomoke and, to the north, the Susquehannock.

As English colonists took their land in the 1700s, many Nanticoke moved north. Some joined the Haudenosaunee in New York and others the Lenape. Those who stayed formed the Nanticoke Indian Tribe of Millsboro, Delaware.
